primitives.name: Optimistic Concurrency Control Transition
primitives.verbatim_quote: --name: xxx-occ-transition description: Implement or audit optimistic-concurrency-controlled XXX state mutations.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V': 'version number (dimensionless)', 'A': 'aggregate ID (UUID-like string)', 'T': 'transition type (enum)', 'E': 'evidence hash (SHA-256)', 'K': 'idempotency key (string)'}
primitives.assumptions: Two or more actors may concurrently read and attempt to mutate the same state version.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When concurrent writes occur, OCC detects conflicts via version mismatch and aborts conflicting transactions.

layer2.mapping: State transition function f(V, A, T, E, K) → V' maps input parameters to updated version; conflict resolution mirrors Bayesian update on policy constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Transaction commit success rate, conflict frequency, and rollback count per aggregate.

primitives.name: Atomic Versioned Update Predicate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Update with a version predicate, increment exactly once, and require one affected row.
primitives.latex: \forall i \in \mathbb{Z}: \text{UPDATE } R \text{ SET } V = V + 1 \text{ WHERE } V = v_i \text{ AND } \text{ROW\_COUNT} = 1
primitives.assumptions: Each update must be uniquely tied to a known previous version to prevent lost updates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when ROW_COUNT ≠ 1 due to concurrent modification.

layer2.mapping: Predicate-based update kernel ensures serializability by requiring exact version match before incrementing.
layer2.telemetry: Version predicate match rate, failed update counts, and average retry attempts.

primitives.name: Policy Validated Commit
primitives.verbatim_quote: Commit only after every invariant succeeds; otherwise roll back and return the typed conflict or policy error.
primitives.latex: \text{IF } \forall p \in P: \text{inv}(p, s) \text{ THEN COMMIT ELSE ROLLBACK}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'set of policy invariants (boolean predicates)', 's': 'state vector (tuple)', 'inv(p, s)': 'policy validation function returning boolean'}
primitives.assumptions: All invariants must hold true at commit time to ensure semantic correctness.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Commit fails if any invariant evaluates to false, triggering rollback and error propagation.

layer2.mapping: Commit kernel applies logical conjunction of all policy checks to determine final state acceptance.
layer2.telemetry: Invariant pass/fail ratio, commit latency, and policy violation types.

reasoning_traces.think:
The OCC framework operates as a dual-state system: read phase validates initial conditions against versioned state, while write phase enforces atomicity via predicate-based updates. The core mathematical duality lies between conflict detection (via version mismatch) and resolution (via rollback and retry). Each transition is modeled as a deterministic function f(V, A, T, E, K) → V', where inputs define a unique state evolution path. Policy validation acts as a constraint layer, ensuring that only semantically valid transitions proceed. Failure modes include lost updates (when version predicates fail) and race conditions (if retries do not re-read). The system's robustness hinges on idempotency keys and fenced side-effect logs to maintain exactly-once semantics despite OCC’s limitations in guaranteeing side-effect uniqueness.
